lens: The evidence pool reveals a recurring motif: exercise-induced molecular responses are pathway- and subgroup-specific rather than uniformly beneficial, yet nearly all studies report aggregate endpoints. The most publishable framing is not 'exercise reduces inflammation' but rather the divergence between which inflammatory axes (CRP/IL6 vs TNF-pathway vs angiocrine factors like PEDF/VEGF) are preferentially modulated by exercise alone versus combination interventions, and how this specificity is further distorted by obesity-related anabolic resistance and disease-state vascular dysfunction.
known_to_ignore: Exercise reduces inflammatory biomarkers in cancer survivors
Voluntary running reduces tumor growth in mouse xenograft models
Exercise capacity inversely correlates with mortality risk
Diet plus exercise reduces angiogenic and coagulation factors in postmenopausal women
tensions: Exercise alone robustly reduces hs-CRP/IL6 (facts 6, 8: -30%) but does NOT reduce sTNFαR2; only the exercise+metformin arm achieves sTNFαR2 reduction (fact 5: -13.1%), suggesting metformin unlocks a TNF-pathway gate that exercise cannot breach alone — yet both interventions share the same cancer survivor population (Cancer Prev Res 2020).

Lean rats show +34% mixed-muscle protein synthesis post-resistance exercise while obese Zucker rats show -7% (fact 14), a 41-percentage-point anabolic resistance gap, yet the only human synthesis data (facts 1, 2) are from healthy young men with no body-composition stratification — making cross-species translation to obese exercise prescription precarious.

Both VEGF (-10%) and PEDF (-10%) decline with diet+exercise in postmenopausal women (facts 11, 12), yet PEDF is endogenously anti-angiogenic while VEGF is pro-angiogenic — the concurrent suppression suggests net angiocrine remodeling rather than simple anti-angiogenesis, which may or may not be the mechanism behind the 66% tumor suppression seen in voluntary wheel-running mice (fact 3).
gaps: No human data exist on muscle protein fractional synthetic rate stratified by obesity status after exercise — fact 14 is limited to Zucker rats, while facts 1-2 exclude obese participants entirely.

The metformin-plus-exercise cancer survivor trial (facts 5-8) does not report whether sTNFαR2 reduction predicts recurrence-free survival, leaving the clinical meaning of pathway-specific inflammation suppression unresolved.
No trial has tested NIRS-derived SmO2-guided exercise prescription in PAD (fact 10 shows -54% SmO2 drop) as a precision dosing tool for claudication rehabilitation.
Isosorbide dinitrate + voluntary exercise synergy for muscle mass (fact 16: +25%) has only been demonstrated in aged female mice with no human pharmacological exercise-priming trial.

The IGF-I/IGFBP-3 ratio increase (+5.4%, fact 9) with diet+exercise in postmenopausal women has not been linked mechanistically to concurrent PEDF/VEGF/PAI-1 changes (facts 11-13) despite overlapping cohorts.

theses.title: Pathway-specific anti-inflammatory gating: metformin unlocks TNF-axis suppression in exercise-responsive cancer survivors that exercise alone cannot achieve
theses.rationale: Facts 5-8 from the same Cancer Prevention Research 2020 trial demonstrate that exercise alone targets CRP/IL6 (-30%) but only exercise+metformin reaches sTNFαR2 (-13.1%), implying pharmacological gating of a distinct inflammatory arm. A scoping review mapping exercise-oncology trials that separately report TNF-pathway vs CRP/IL6 endpoints could formalize this pathway-divergence as a combinatory design principle.

theses.title: Obesity-induced anabolic resistance to exercise: cross-species evidence synthesis and implications for dose escalation in obese humans
theses.rationale: The 41-percentage-point gap between lean (+34%) and obese Zucker rat (-7%) protein synthetic responses to resistance exercise (fact 14) versus the +42-69% responses in lean young men (facts 1-2) constitutes an evidence gap with direct clinical implications: current exercise prescriptions for obese individuals may be sub-threshold for anabolic signaling. An evidence-gap paper would justify RCTs stratifying protein synthesis by BMI in humans.

theses.title: Concurrent PEDF and VEGF suppression by lifestyle intervention: toward a net-angiocrine-remodeling hypothesis for exercise-mediated tumor control
theses.rationale: The parallel ~10% reductions in both pro-angiogenic VEGF and anti-angiogenic PEDF (facts 11, 12) alongside PAI-1 suppression (fact 13) in postmenopausal women, when juxtaposed with 66% tumor reduction from voluntary running in mice (fact 3), challenge a simple 'exercise starves tumors via VEGF reduction' narrative. A mechanistic perspective paper could argue for a net-angiocrine-remodeling framework integrating PAI-1-mediated fibrinolytic shifts.

theses.title: NO-donor pharmacological priming of exercise-induced hypertrophy in sarcopenia: from aged mouse muscle to translational trial design
theses.rationale: Fact 16 shows a 25% muscle mass increase from isosorbide dinitrate + voluntary exercise in 18-month-old female mice, yet no human trial has tested NO-donor exercise-priming in sarcopenic adults. A pilot meta-analysis pooling existing nitrate supplementation exercise trials (with muscle mass endpoints) could estimate feasibility and effect sizes for a definitive RCT in older adults.

reviewer_objections: Facts 1-2 and fact 14 compare protein synthesis across species (human vs Zucker rat) and exercise modalities (BFR vs resistance) — any cross-species synthesis argument lacks direct head-to-head evidence and risks ecological fallacy.

The metformin+exercise vs exercise-alone inflammatory comparison (facts 5-8) derives from a single trial in cancer survivors without type 2 diabetes; generalizability to diabetic cancer survivors or non-cancer populations is speculative.

Concurrent PEDF and VEGF suppression (facts 11-12) could reflect weight loss per se rather than exercise, since both study arms included caloric restriction (225 min/week activity + 10% weight-loss goal) — the independent exercise contribution cannot be isolated from these facts alone.

The SmO2 finding (fact 10) uses a single fatiguing bout protocol in PAD patients; whether chronic exercise training normalizes this deficit is unknown, making any clinical dosing recommendation premature.

Fact 16 (NO-donor + exercise) uses a combined intervention without a NO-donor-only or exercise-only arm visible in the evidence pool, preventing attribution of the 25% muscle mass gain to the synergy rather than either component alone.
next_extractions: Protein fractional synthetic rate data stratified by BMI or body-fat percentage in human exercise trials
sTNFαR2 changes in exercise-only arms of oncology RCTs beyond the Cancer Prevention Research 2020 trial
NIRS-derived SmO2 or muscle oxygenation responses across exercise training durations in PAD cohorts
Nitrate or NO-donor supplementation trials with lean-mass or muscle cross-sectional area endpoints in adults ≥65 years
Individual-level data linking PEDF/VEGF/PAI-1 changes to tumor incidence or recurrence in postmenopausal lifestyle intervention cohorts
